subject: Unexpected overage: ingest aliasing causing duplicate token charges — VAT impact
messages:
From: Mike Chen <mike@orbitlabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah@orbitlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:12:00 -0800
Subject: Spike on Nov 4–6 + VAT line question

Hi Neha,

We noticed an unexpected charge on our Nov invoice — a sharp spike during Nov 4–6 that doesn't match our activity dashboard. I'm attaching our exported usage report (usage_report_OrbitLabs_Nov.csv) and a small token dump we pulled from our ingestion pipeline (redwood_token_dump_snippet.txt). It looks like several sessions from our bulk ingestion job were re-sent with slightly different client-side IDs; token counts appear duplicated in Redwood's metering.

Two asks: 1) can you explain why these duplicate tokens were counted on your side and 2) if there is a retroactive credit, how will the VAT line be handled on the corrected invoice? We need to reconcile this with our finance team for month-end.

Thanks — would prefer a short call if helpful.

— Mike
Mike Chen
Head of Platform
Orbit Labs
phone: +1 415 555 0198

Attachment stubs: usage_report_OrbitLabs_Nov.csv (CSV), redwood_token_dump_snippet.txt (text)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Mike Chen <mike@orbitlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike on Nov 4–6 + VAT line question

Hi Mike — thanks for the note and the files. I've looped in Ben from billing and Lauren who owns the Orbit relationship.

Quick triage notes:
- We see an ingest pattern consistent with duplicate sessions where client-side request IDs changed on retries; our metering dedup window is per-request-id by default, so differing client ids can lead to duplicate token counts.
- We will pull the matching request ids and tokenization map for the Nov 4–6 window to confirm whether these are genuine duplicates or tokenization differences (e.g., newline normalization or UTF variants).

Can you confirm if the bulk job used your retry logic between 03:00–05:00 UTC on Nov 5? If so, please grant us permission to pull the example request IDs referenced in your snippet.

We will also put the disputed portion of the invoice on hold pending investigation — Ben, please advise on the hold/credit process.

I can schedule a 30-min sync later this week if useful.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Revenue Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mike Chen <mike@orbitlabs.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike on Nov 4–6 + VAT line question

Mike — thanks for flagging this and for the attachments. We're placing the disputed $12,480 line item on hold for now (invoice #INV-20261107-ORB). Pending the technical review, we'll provisionally apply a proforma credit to your account so your month-end cash reconciliation isn't blocked.

Process & next steps:
- Technical triage (Neha + infra) will confirm root cause by EOD Thu Nov 12.
- If we confirm duplicate metering due to client-side retry id variance, we will post a corrective invoice and a VAT-corrected credit memo.
- Treasury needs Orbit's billing contact to push the credit; please confirm the email for your AP team (we currently have finance@orbitlabs.com).

I've attached an interim usage extract from our side showing the suspect sessions (interim_extract_20261109.csv). If you want an immediate partial credit we can issue a provisional adjustment after we have minimal confirmation.

— Ben

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: VAT handling on corrective credits

Hi all — quick note from tax: if we issue a retroactive credit, we need Orbit's legal entity and VAT ID to produce an adjusted invoice that preserves the VAT reporting trail. For EU-registered entities we issue a credit memo that includes the VAT reversal line; for non-EU we remove the VAT component. Please provide:
- Legal entity name on file
- VAT/GST ID (if applicable)
- Invoice numbers to adjust (Ben referenced INV-20261107-ORB)

If we end up issuing multiple small credits, we prefer to aggregate them into a single corrective credit memo to minimize bookkeeping noise.

— Rishi
Tax & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Mike Chen <mike@orbitlabs.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Spike on Nov 4–6 + VAT line question

Thanks, everyone — appreciate the quick turn.

Answers:
- Our AP contact for credits: finance@orbitlabs.com (Claire Zhang, accounts payable).
- Legal entity: Orbit Labs, Inc. — US company, no EU VAT ID.
- Invoice to adjust: INV-20261107-ORB (same as you noted).

We grant Redwood permission to pull the request IDs referenced in the snippet and to correlate them against your metering logs. The bulk job did have retry logic between 03:00–05:00 UTC on Nov 5; looks like a recent deploy changed the client request id format.

Call is fine — Wed 11/11 at 10:00 PT worked for us; Claire will join if helpful. Please send the invite.

— Mike
